subject: generating estimated yearly site abundances from pcountOpen model and predict()

messages.author: 13fa979ab1568be1
messages.subject: generating estimated yearly site abundances from pcountOpen model and predict()
parts:
Hi colleagues,

I'm fitting the following open point count model with 8 primary and 8
secondary periods.

x.umf <- unmarkedFramePCO(y=x.dat[,1:64],

siteCovs= data.frame(x.dat[,c("BLOCK", "TREATMENT")]),
obsCovs= list(OBSEXP = x.dat[,names(x.dat)[83:146]]),
yearlySiteCovs = list(LOGGED = x.dat[,names(x.dat)[67:74]],
YEAR = x.dat[,names(x.dat)[75:82]]),
numPrimary=8)

(fm1 <- pcountOpen(~BLOCK, ~LOGGED + TREATMENT + YEAR, ~LOGGED +
TREATMENT + YEAR, ~OBSEXP, x.umf, K=30))

Predictions are then generated as follows:

lambda <- predict(fm1, type="lambda")[,1] # abundance at each site
gamma <- predict(fm1, type="gamma")[,1] # recruitment rate
omega <- predict(fm1, type="omega")[,1] # apparent survival rate

lambda is Mx1, gamma is M(T-1) and omega is M(T-1) where M is the
number of sites and T is the number of primary sampling periods
(years). I would like to construct a MxT matrix that contains
estimated abundance for each site and year but having trouble
identifying the elements of omega and gamma because each is a long
list with 7 times the number of stations. My understanding is the
following general algorithm is used:

N(1) = lambda
N(t) = N(t-1)*omega + gamma

A simple or not so simple way to construct the MxT matrix of estimated
abundance would be greatly appreciated. I've unfortunately not been
able to find documentation on what is generated by predict() in terms
of gamma and omega. - Thanks in advance

Scott

messages.author: 527e14923215b7e4
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] generating estimated yearly site abundances from pcountOpen model and predict()
parts:
Hi Scott,

To correctly format the predictions as a matrix, you can do this:

gamma.mat <- matrix(gamma, M, T-1, byrow=TRUE)

You are right that this should be documented better.

Also, have you tried ranef() and bup() in the new version of unmarked? These are more appropriate for finite-sample inference.

Richard
